muxt generate --use-datastar --use-receiver-type=Server
muxt check

exec go test -count=1

-- template.gohtml --
{{- define "GET /users Page(ctx)" -}}
<div data-init="{{ .Actions.Refresh | .JS }}"></div>
<button data-on:click="{{ .Actions.CreateUser | .JS }}">create</button>
<button data-on:click="{{ .Actions.UpdateUser 42 | .JS }}">save</button>
<button data-on:click="{{ .Actions.ReplaceUser 42 | .JS }}">replace</button>
<button data-on:click="{{ .Actions.DeleteUser 42 | .JS }}">delete</button>
{{- end -}}
{{- define "GET /refresh Refresh(ctx)" -}}ok{{- end -}}
{{- define "POST /users CreateUser(ctx)" -}}ok{{- end -}}
{{- define "PATCH /users/{id} UpdateUser(ctx, id)" -}}ok{{- end -}}
{{- define "PUT /users/{id} ReplaceUser(ctx, id)" -}}ok{{- end -}}
{{- define "DELETE /users/{id} DeleteUser(ctx, id)" -}}ok{{- end -}}
-- go.mod --
module server

go 1.24
-- template.go --
package server

import (
	"context"
	"embed"
	"html/template"
)

//go:embed *.gohtml
var templatesFS embed.FS

var templates = template.Must(template.ParseFS(templatesFS, "*"))

// Server wires a page's buttons to its own routes: each action renders a
// verb-correct Datastar backend-action expression from what muxt knows
// statically, so markup cannot drift from the route table.
type Server struct{}

func (Server) Page(_ context.Context) (string, error) { return "", nil }

func (Server) Refresh(_ context.Context) (string, error) { return "", nil }

func (Server) CreateUser(_ context.Context) (string, error) { return "", nil }

func (Server) UpdateUser(_ context.Context, id int) (string, error) { return "", nil }

func (Server) ReplaceUser(_ context.Context, id int) (string, error) { return "", nil }

func (Server) DeleteUser(_ context.Context, id int) (string, error) { return "", nil }
-- template_test.go --
package server

import (
	"net/http"
	"net/http/httptest"
	"strings"
	"testing"
)

func Test(t *testing.T) {
	mux := http.NewServeMux()
	TemplateRoutes(mux, Server{})

	req := httptest.NewRequest(http.MethodGet, "/users", nil)
	rec := httptest.NewRecorder()
	mux.ServeHTTP(rec, req)

	body := rec.Body.String()
	// The expression is unquoted (template.JS — a plain string would render
	// JSON-quoted and Datastar would not execute it) and the apostrophes
	// carry standard HTML attribute escaping, which the browser decodes
	// before Datastar reads the attribute; verb inferred per route.
	for _, want := range []string{
		`data-init="@get(&#39;/refresh&#39;)"`,
		`data-on:click="@post(&#39;/users&#39;)"`,
		`data-on:click="@patch(&#39;/users/42&#39;)"`,
		`data-on:click="@put(&#39;/users/42&#39;)"`,
		`data-on:click="@delete(&#39;/users/42&#39;)"`,
	} {
		if !strings.Contains(body, want) {
			t.Errorf("body = %q, want it to contain %q", body, want)
		}
	}
	if strings.Contains(body, `"&#34;@`) || strings.Contains(body, `="\"@`) {
		t.Errorf("body = %q; the action must not render as a quoted JS string literal", body)
	}
}
